name: Idaho Falls Auditorium District
tax_rate: 5% IFAD auditorium district tax on short-term lodging inside district boundaries (Idaho Falls), collected by the Idaho State Tax Commission (Form 4150); stacks on the 6% state sales tax and the 2% state travel and convention tax for 13% on a room
deadline_pattern: No grant program; all room-tax revenue is committed to the Mountain America Center (Hero Arena) financing and operations
annual_pool: FY2026 Tax Commission distributions to IFAD about $3.23M gross; none of it is offered to outside applicants
contact: Idaho Falls Auditorium District office (208) 932-2729 (Idaho State Tax Commission listing); Rob Spear, Executive Director (hired April 2019); Mountain America Center venue office (986) 497-0509, info@mountainamericacenter.com, 1690 Event Center Drive, Idaho Falls, ID 83402
notes: Voters created the district in May 2011 (63% yes) with a 5% room tax to build an event center; the $62M Mountain America Center opened November 2022 and is run by Centennial Management. The room tax services the center's certificates of participation (about $40M planned) and operations, so the board does not run a grant or sponsorship round. Outside event producers deal with the venue as a client, not as grantees; tourism grant dollars in the region flow through the Idaho Travel Council grant to Yellowstone Teton Territory.

name: Sandpoint
tax_rate: 14% Resort City Tax on hotels, bed and breakfasts and short-term vacation rentals (7% base plus an additional 7% for streets and pedestrian improvements approved Nov 8, 2022, effective Jan 1, 2023 through Dec 31, 2035); plus 6% state sales tax and 2% state travel and convention tax (22% total on a room). A separate 1% general local option sales tax (parks, 2021) excludes nothing lodging-specific; a new 1% streets LOT (Jan 1, 2027 to Dec 31, 2036) was on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot and failed per unofficial local reporting
deadline_pattern: No application process; the council allocates resort city tax in the annual budget (public hearing in August) to public safety, parks, the SPOT bus, streets and property tax relief
annual_pool: City budgeted $1.5M of resort city tax in FY2023 and FY2024 (collections had been $558K to $615K at the old 7% rate); FY2024 collections came in under budget, so no property tax relief was budgeted for FY2025
contact: Sarah Lynds, Finance Director, 208-263-3557; Resort City Tax Specialist and Assistant Finance Director via Finance Department, City of Sandpoint, 1123 W. Lake Street, Sandpoint, ID 83864; Mayor Jeremy Grimm, 208-263-3310
notes: Sandpoint's resort city tax is Idaho's largest city lodging tax by rate, but the proceeds are used in-house: the original 7% has historically covered the SPOT bus contract, police and fire shares, parks grounds, lifeguards and Memorial Field, with over-collections going to a property tax relief fund (Ord. 1317), and the added 7% is earmarked for street and sidewalk projects (part of a $7.26M street program in FY2026). No tourism grant, chamber contract or event sponsorship line is funded from it. A 1% streets sales tax on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot failed (unofficial), after a similar measure fell short of 60% in Nov 2024.
meeting_schedule: City Council meets the first and third Wednesdays; budget hearing in mid-August (Aug 20, 2025 for FY2026); fiscal year Oct 1 to Sept 30
pool_note: $1.5M budgeted resort city tax (FY2024 budget; FY2026 figure not broken out in the preliminary budget memo). All of it is allocated to city services, streets and property tax relief; $0 open to outside applicants.

name: Sun Valley
tax_rate: 4% LOT on occupancy sales under 30 days (3% base plus 0.5% for air service and 0.5% for housing, Ords. 484, 572, 573); 4% food and beverage, alcohol by the drink, recreation memberships, rentals and event admissions; 3% other retail; 2% building materials and lift tickets; renewed Nov 4, 2025 with no rate change (420 yes, 68.97%); plus 6% state sales tax and 2% state travel and convention tax (12% on a room)
deadline_pattern: No formal application; outside organizations bring funding requests to the City Council's regular meeting at the start of July during budget development (July 2, 2026 for FY2027), the council sets the tentative budget in late July and holds the budget hearing in early August (Aug 7, 2025 for FY2026); larger one-off asks such as the FIS World Cup are heard in November and December as separate service contracts
typical_open: Spring; requests should reach City Administrator Jim Keating before the June budget workshops so they can be heard at the early-July council meeting
annual_pool: No set pool. FY2027 requests heard July 2026: Mountain Rides $498,000, 2027 FIS Ski World Cup Finals organizing committee $233,000, Sun Valley Economic Development $8,500, Blaine County Emergency Communication Center (amount not reported); council also allocated $320,000 to Visit Sun Valley in the FY2027 budget review (Aug 2026). FY2025: Sun Valley Co. World Cup sponsorship up to $214,000 (plus $93,900 city costs) against a $500,000 budget line
contact: Jim Keating, City Administrator; Nancy Flannigan, City Clerk/Asst. to the City Administrator, nflannigan@sunvalleyidaho.gov; Andrea Perez, Assistant City Clerk/Assistant Finance Manager, aperez@sunvalleyidaho.gov; City Hall 208-622-4438, 81 Elkhorn Road, P.O. Box 416, Sun Valley, ID 83353
notes: Sun Valley funds outside groups through annual service contracts rather than a grant round, because Idaho cities cannot simply donate money. LOT (about $3.0M in FY2025, of which $1.37M lodging) goes to the general fund and underwrites those contracts, and the council explicitly weighs LOT return when it sponsors events: it approved up to $214,000 for Sun Valley Co.'s March 2025 World Cup Finals expecting about $200,000 in extra LOT, and heard a $233,000 request for the March 20-25, 2027 Finals in July 2026. Requests are heard at the early-July council meeting and folded into the budget adopted in August for the fiscal year starting Oct 1. The pooled 0.5% air-service LOT is allocated separately by the Sun Valley Air Service Board (mayors of Sun Valley, Ketchum and Hailey), mostly to Visit Sun Valley.

name: Ketchum
tax_rate: 3% on room sales and short-term rentals under 30 days (2% Original LOT plus 1% Additional LOT split 0.5% air service / 0.5% housing, Ord. 1244, through mid-2028); 3% liquor by the drink; 2% other retail and building materials; plus 6% state sales tax and 2% state travel and convention tax (11% on a room). Original LOT expires Dec 31, 2027; the Nov 3, 2026 renewal (Ord. 1282: 4% lodging, 1.5% retail and building materials, 2027-2041) got 52.96% yes (1,063 to 944) and failed the 60% threshold
deadline_pattern: No application process; the council sets Original LOT allocations in the annual budget (workshops June, budget ordinance readings in August, FY starts Oct 1) and renews the same contract partners each year
annual_pool: Original LOT Fund FY2027 $3,870,000 (FY2025 actual revenue $4,097,253): Events/Promotions $120,000, Wagon Days transfer $224,700, Ketchum Arts & Heritage Commission $35,000, Sun Valley Economic Development $15,000, Friends of the Sawtooth Avalanche Center $10,000, Idaho Dark Sky Alliance $3,000, Mountain Humane $3,000, Mountain Rides $878,000, dispatch $185,000, public safety reimbursement $1,322,700, capital $1,038,600
contact: Ketchum Taxes, taxes@ketchumidaho.org, 208-726-3841, P.O. Box 2315, 191 5th Street West, Ketchum, ID 83340; Brent Davis, Director of Finance/Treasurer; Jade Riley, City Administrator; Daniel Hansen, city spokesman
notes: Ketchum's Original LOT (about $3.8M to $4.1M a year) is budgeted by category: 39% emergency services, 27% capital, 22% Mountain Rides, 9% events (a $120,000 Events/Promotions line plus the city-run Wagon Days festival, which gets 65% of its cost from LOT) and 2% partnerships to a fixed set of nonprofits. There is no open grant round; a new event would have to negotiate services or sponsorship with the city (Ketchum offered up to $155,000 in services for the 2025 World Cup Finals). The Nov 3, 2026 renewal-and-increase measure failed at 52.96%, so the city plans a second attempt in Nov 2027; if that also fails the LOT and its event funding end Dec 31, 2027.

name: Donnelly
tax_rate: 3% hotel, motel and short-term occupancy tax (hotel and motel rooms, condos, tourist homes, campgrounds) plus 1% municipal sales tax on retail; Donnelly City Code 3.10, Ord. 247 (2019), 10-year term with first payments February 2020; plus 6% state sales tax and 2% state travel and convention tax
deadline_pattern: Applications due in mid-April for the fiscal year starting the following Oct 1 (April 14, 2025 for FY2026; April 16, 2026 for FY2027); the five-member LOT Committee meets within a week or two of the deadline (May 6, 2025; April 22, 2026) and the council adopts the recommendations at its May meeting (May 19, 2025; May 18, 2026); next deadline expected mid-April 2027 for FY2028
typical_open: Application form posted in February (FY26 form posted Feb 2025); submit by email to the City Clerk
annual_pool: FY2026 awards approved May 19, 2025: $372,894.98 total; FY2027 awards approved May 18, 2026: about $223,810 (figure partly garbled in the packet); LOT expense budget line $350,000 a year; 21 or more applications were ranked in the FY2027 round
contact: Lori Clemens, City Clerk/Treasurer, lclemens@cityofdonnelly.org, (208) 325-8859, P.O. Box 725, 169 Halferty Street, Donnelly, ID 83615
notes: Donnelly runs the only true open application round among Idaho's small resort cities. Under code 3.10.060 a council-appointed commission of five business or property owners holds one meeting a year to hear every request, then the council adopts the ranked list; for-profit, nonprofit and government applicants may apply in ten categories including economic growth, marketing and promotion, recreational and cultural events, grant matches, parks and public safety. Awards can be paid upfront under an agreement or by reimbursement, and all advertising must credit the City of Donnelly Local Option Tax. The FY2027 round (deadline April 16, 2026) was approved May 18, 2026 with applications #20 and #21 swapped, so expect 20+ competing requests; recipients have included Donnelly Pathways, Donnelly Elementary and the Donnelly Firefighters.

deadline_pattern: No grant program found; stated uses are bridges, capital projects, infrastructure, pathways and parks, transportation, visitor services and public safety

notes: Swan Valley is a 300-person gateway town on the South Fork of the Snake whose tax base is fly-fishing lodges and vacation rentals. Its LOT has been renewed in short terms (Nov 2020, Nov 2021) and a seven-year renewal was on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot alongside a 3% occupancy tax for neighboring Irwin; Bonneville County's cumulative results PDF (11-4-2026) could not be fetched, so the outcome is unconfirmed. deadline_pattern: No grant program; uses are limited to fire, law enforcement, streets, sidewalks, buildings and grounds, and property tax relief
contact: Bonners Ferry City Hall, 7232 Main Street, PO Box 149, Bonners Ferry, ID 83805, 208-267-3105
notes: Bonners Ferry's 1% LOT is a general sales tax that happens to reach lodging; the ordinance restricts spending to fire, police, streets and facilities with over-collections to property tax relief, so there is no tourism purpose and no application. tax_rate: 5% on lodging (30 days or less), 3% liquor by the drink, 1% prepared meals, 0.5% other qualifying retail sales; Ord. 2025-05, approved Nov 2025 (about 75% yes, after failing by two votes in 2024), effective Jan 1, 2026 for 10 years; plus 6% state sales tax and 2% state travel and convention tax

notes: Idaho's newest resort city LOT, in force since Jan 1, 2026. Permitted uses are transportation and infrastructure (water, sewer, parks), facilities, visitor services, grant programs and property tax relief, so a small grant round is possible once the council sees a year of receipts, but nothing exists yet. Watch the FY2027 budget (adopted Aug-Sept 2026) and the FY2028 budget for a first allocation; Teton Valley events otherwise work through the Teton Valley Chamber and Yellowstone Teton Territory.
